subtype: Approach: hero engineer who refuses help [Pitfall]
passage:
Ayesha: Indu, it's been five hours. Want me to take the logs for a bit?
Indu: I've got it. Explaining would take longer than doing it.
Ayesha: Then at least sleep an hour. I'll page you.
Indu: No. Almost there 🙂
[two hours later]
Indu: oops
Indu: I ran the wrong command on the live database. It needs a restart from scratch.
Ayesha: Okay. Don't touch anything else. I'm calling the on-call lead now.
Indu: sorry. I should have handed over hours ago 😔
Ayesha: Send me exactly what you ran. We'll sort it.
[The site stayed down until morning.]

qa.q: What did Indu do that lengthened the outage?
qa.a: Indu ran the wrong command on the live database.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling in the last messages?
qa.a: Indu felt regretful and embarrassed, apologising and admitting that a handover was due hours earlier. 😔

qa.q: What could Indu have done differently?
qa.a: Indu could have handed over the logs and rested, since a rested teammate might have caught the mistake or avoided it.

qa.q: How might Ayesha have felt when Indu turned down help?
qa.a: Ayesha was probably worried and a little sidelined, having offered twice and been refused.

grounding: Shows a senior engineer refusing help for hours until fatigue causes a wrong command that prolongs the outage.
